highlights.text: Two distinct roots:
al-ṣayf — the season after late spring (summer)
Ibn Fāris identifies two distinct genuine meanings under the root Ṭ-L-Ḥ:
Al-ṭalḥ is a well-known tree species; one single tree is a ṭalḥa.
Core sense: a patch on something that differs in color from the rest of it.
al-baraṣ — the skin condition (vitiligo/leprosy-like patches) that gives the root its name.
One core meaning: cutting something short — before it is completed.
a man with no surviving offspring (to carry on his line) is called abtar
Hadith citation: "kill the two-striped [snake] and the short-tailed [abtar] one"
whose core meaning is leaving a thing out of inadvertence or heedlessness
to be heedless of / neglect" something, i.e. to leave it because you have forgotten it (sāhiyan)
a single core meaning that branches into two senses
The passive form ghīḍa is used specifically when the diminishing is caused by something else acting on it
One core meaning: the bringing-down of a structure; further senses are measured against it.
hadamtu al-ḥāʾiṭa — I demolished the wall
a hadith formula, "al-damu al-damu, wa al-hadamu al-hadam," is cited and glossed as a treaty pledge of shared life and shared death
a root meaning agitation and motion in a thing
hazaztu l-qanāt: I shook the spear-shaft, and it quivered (ihtazzat)
Plants ihtazza (stir), and the wind hazza them (shakes them)
a set of things gathered together, held, and kept for use
is the goods and equipment of a household
the Arabs say ضَرَبَ فِي جَهَازِهِ — literally "it struck out into its own gear,"
a single core idea: sufficiency — a measure that is enough, with nothing further needed or sought beyond it
the flashing or gleaming (lamʿ) of something
lamḥah being a single instance of that flash
a verse describes watching for "a lamḥ [flash/glimpse] of Suhayl [the star Canopus],"
it consists of two unrelated words sharing the same letters
"lā yalitkum min aʿmālikum shayʾan" — "He will not diminish you anything of your deeds."
three senses he regards as diverging from one another in derivation
al-muzn - "rain-cloud"; a single cloud-mass is a muznah.
a single sound root whose core meaning is rising up and appearing / becoming visible
To rise or come up: نَجَمَ النَّجْمُ ("the star/najm rose")
the nun-kaf-sin root signals turning something upside-down (inverting it).
Al-naks - the basic verbal noun: turning a thing over onto its head.
the root is a single, sound (unweakened) root meaning "breaking" (al-kasr)
Verb: qaṣamtu al-shay' qaṣman — "I broke the thing."
al-qunūṭ is despair of good, i.e. giving up hope that good will come.
"So do not be among the despairing" (al-Ḥijr 15:55)
the intensive form qanūṭ paired with yaʾūs
three separate, unrelated roots rather than one core idea
where the noun رُقِيّ is the act of going up.
the proverb ارْقَ عَلَى ظَلْعِكَ, literally "climb according to your lameness,"
core meaning is confinement / imprisonment (al-ḥabs)
the place in which a person is confined.
a line by Ibn Muqbil, "a striking the champions enjoined
weaponry: that with which fighting is carried out
a line of verse describing horses scowling as they bear the champions, "rising with the Indian blades and the shields"
mixing/intermixing one thing with another.
a whip comes into contact with / mingles against the skin when striking
a share/portion (of the punishment)
the dirt/grime that collects under a trimmed nail
glosses tafath here as "their dirt" (wasakh)
a Bedouin's saying, mā atfathaka wa-adranaka ("How grimy and filthy you are!")
whose core meaning is the joining or connecting of one thing to another.
derives waṣiyya — an injunction or bequest — from this same idea
both meaning "to enjoin/charge someone."
one single underlying notion: al-watid, "the peg" or "stake" (the kind driven into the ground, e.g. a tent-peg)
Core sense — the peg itself, and the verb of driving one in.
a single sound root whose one idea is dryness.
يَبِسَ ("to dry out, become dry")
a place that the water withdraws from, so that it dries out
